question.problem: The $8$th and $9$th terms of an arithmetic sequence are $17$ and $21,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$ 

Since the terms ${a}_{8}=17$ and ${a}_{9}=21$ are consecutive, we can subtract them to find the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{9}-{a}_{8} \\  & =21-17 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{8}=17,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{8}$ is $7$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{8} & ={a}_{1}+7d \\ 17 & ={a}_{1}+7(4) \\ 17 & ={a}_{1}+28 \\ 17-28 & ={a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =-11\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-11+(n-1)(4) \\  & =-11+4n-4 \\  & =4n-15\end{aligned}
$$
